questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs
- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications
- Validation via audit logs and Gatekeeper status

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:
  name: restrict-api-verbs
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

## Validation Plan
1. Deploy ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
2. Test compliant GET request from approved SPIFFE ID
3. Test noncompliant POST request from unapproved SPIFFE ID
4. Verify denial in Gatekeeper audit logs
5. Confirm monitoring namespace bypass works correctly

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests policy-as-code skills for multi-tenant Kubernetes environments
- Evaluates ability to translate security requirements into enforceable runtime and CI gates

Key Concepts
- Kyverno, Pod Security Standards, Resource limits, CI gates, Drift detection

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deployments
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must define a secure securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and drop all capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: "true"
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
  - name: require-resources
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must specify resource limits and requests"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
```

Failing Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: insecure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "64Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
          limits:
            memory: "128Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
```

CI Validation Steps
```bash
# Install Kyverno CLI
brew install kyverno

# Validate policies against manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest deployment.yaml

# CI/CD integration example (GitHub Actions)
- name: Validate Kubernetes manifests
  run: |
    kyverno apply policy.yaml -f deploy/
```

Runtime Gate Demonstration
```bash
# Apply the policy cluster-wide
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Verify policy is active
kubectl get clusterpolicy require-secure-deployments

# Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest (will fail)
kubectl apply -f insecure-deployment.yaml
# Error: Validation failed: Each container must define a secure securityContext...

# Deploy compliant manifest (will succeed)
kubectl apply -f secure-deployment.yaml
# deployment.apps/secure-app created
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of Kubernetes manifests is a practical, repeatable gate in real projects. This tests understanding of policy-as-code, tooling choices (Kyverno vs Gatekeeper), constraint design for host access controls and image source controls, and CI integration in GitHub Actions with ephemeral test clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper
- Constraints for host access (hostNetwork, hostPath, hostPort, privileged containers)
- Image source controls (allowed registries) and imagePullPolicy enforcement
- CI integration in GitHub Actions using KinD or similar ephemeral clusters

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-host-access
spec:
  rules:
  - name: block-host-network
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork is not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
  - name: block-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not allowed"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ contains(element.volumes[].hostPath, '') }}"
          operator: "NotEqual"
          value: ""
```

## Minimal Policy (Combined)
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: security-guardrails
spec:
  rules:
  - name: deny-host-network-port
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork and hostPort are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
          hostPort: "0"
  - name: deny-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not permitted"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ @ }}"
          operator: "AnyNotIn"
          value: [""]
      foreach:
        - list: "spec.volumes[?hostPath]"
          deny: true
  - name: deny-privileged-containers
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Privileged containers are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              privileged: "false"
  - name: allowed-registries
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Images must come from approved registries"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "registry.company.com/*"
            imagePullPolicy: "Always"
```

## Failing Manifest (hostPath + hostNetwork)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: docker.io/myapp:latest
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - name: host-volume
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: host-volume
    hostPath:
      path: /etc
```

## Passing Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.company.com/myapp:v1.0
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Validation
```bash
# Install Kyverno locally
brew install kyverno

# Apply policies
kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml

# Validate a manifest
kyverno validate insecure-pod.yaml
```

## CI Validation (GitHub Actions)
```yaml
name: Validate Manifests
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Create KinD cluster
      run: kind create cluster
    - name: Install Kyverno
      run: |
        kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/releases/latest/download/install.yaml
        kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app=kyverno -n kyverno --timeout=120s
    - name: Apply policies
      run: kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f insecure-pod.yaml || echo "Expected failure"
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f secure-pod.yaml
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to combine SBOM provenance, cryptographic attestation, and admission control in multi-tenant Kubernetes environments with concrete artifacts and workflow.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM provenance (CycloneDX)
- Cosign signatures and Rekor attestations
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Rego policy validation for image attestation and CVE severity

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: ImageSBOMAttestation
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageSBOMAttestation
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package imagesbomattestation
      
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
        container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not valid_image(container.image)
        msg := sprintf("Container image %v fails SBOM/attestation validation", [container.image])
      }
      
      valid_image(image) {
        has_attestation(image)
        no_high_severity_vulns(image)
```

```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions snippet (validation)
name: Validate Provenance
on: [push]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Inspect image for digest and labels
        run: |
          CONTAINER_IMG='registry.example.com/feature-service@sha256:abcdef...'
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' $CONTAINER_IMG | cut -d'@' -f2)
          LABELS=$(docker inspect --format='{{.Config.Labels}}' $CONTAINER_IMG)
          if [[ -z "$DIGEST" || "$LABELS" != *data_version* || "$LABELS" != *model_version* ]]; then
            exit 1

      - name: Canary trace test
        run: |
          # pseudo-step: send request and verify OTLP trace propagates
          curl -sS http://feature-service.canary/health -H 'traceparent: 00-abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789-1234567812345678-01' >/dev/null
          # verification would query OTLP collector for trace-id
          echo 'Canary test passed'
```

```yaml
name: cks-serverless-sign
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Set up Syft for SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v1

      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Verify signature
        run: |
          cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Upload to Rekor
        run: |
          cosign upload blob -f attestation.json
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to enforce Kubernetes scheduling best practices through automated CI gates. It demonstrates understanding of pod distribution for high availability, GitOps workflows, and infrastructure-as-code validation.

## Key Concepts

- **Kubernetes topologySpreadConstraints**: Controls how pods are distributed across failure domains (zones, nodes, etc.)
- **Deployment replicas and scaling**: Understanding when and why to distribute workloads
- **YAML parsing in CI pipelines**: Using Python or Node.js to validate manifests
- **GitHub Actions workflow configuration**: Building automated gates for GitOps
- **Local validation and pre-commit hooks**: Catching issues before code reaches CI

## Code Example

```python
# gate-topology.py
import sys
import yaml
import glob

def check_deploymentConstraints(doc):
    if doc.get('kind') != 'Deployment':
        return True
    
    replicas = doc.get('spec', {}).get('replicas', 1)
    if replicas <= 2:
        return True
    
    topology = doc.get('spec', {}).get('template', {}).get('spec', {})
    if 'topologySpreadConstraints' not in topology:
        return False
    
    for constraint in topology['topologySpreadConstraints']:
        if constraint.get('topologyKey') != 'topology.kubernetes.io/zone':
            return False
        maxSkew = constraint.get('maxSkew', 1)
        if maxSkew > 1:
            return False
    
    return True

def main():
    failed = []
    for manifest in glob.glob('**/*.yaml', recursive=True):
        with open(manifest) as f:
            docs = yaml.safe_load_all(f)
            for doc in docs:
                if doc and not check_deploymentConstraints(doc):
                    failed.append(manifest)
    
    if failed:
        print(f"Failing manifests: {failed}")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    print("All Deployments pass topology constraints check")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## GitHub Actions Workflow

```yaml
name: Topology Constraints Gate
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  enforce-topology:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install pyyaml
      - name: Run topology gate
        run: python gate-topology.py
```

## Failing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:latest
```

## Passing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: web
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:latest
```

## How to Verify

**Local Verification:**
```bash
pip install pyyaml
python gate-topology.py
```

**CI Verification:**
The GitHub Actions workflow runs automatically on pull requests. Merges are blocked until all Deployments with replicas > 2 include proper topologySpreadConstraints.

**Pre-commit Hook:**
Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
```yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: topology-gate
        name: Enforce topologySpreadConstraints
        entry: python gate-topology.py
        language: system
        types: [yaml]
```
